tools.name: clean_extract
tools.description: Extract clean, token-dense markdown from a public URL or raw HTML string, with extraction_status and detailed extraction_quality metadata that identifies empty or probably partial output. The first 3 calls per source IP are free, total, with no header or signup needed; the allowance does not reset.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "clean_extract" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Extract clean, token-dense markdown from a public URL or raw HTML string, with extraction_status and detailed extraction_quality metadata that identifies empty or probably partial output. The first 3 calls per source IP are free, total, with no header or signup needed; the allowance does not reset. " → after: "Extract a full page or selected sections from a public URL or raw HTML. A call is charged only when it returns usable content; the first 3 usable extraction calls are free, total, then USD 0.05. Use the free clean_extract_outline first. Uncharged failures name upstream_timeout, upstream_http_error, "

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
